_comment: All calculation parameters (spec section 6 / 9.2). Every value is a starting value to calibrate. Edit and restart the app.

gainRanges._comment: Per role. maxGain: gain on the simplest project (complexity 0) with full AI enablement. minPotential: gain on the most complex project (complexity 1) with full enablement. floor: gain with no AI enablement (E = 0). Must satisfy floor <= minPotential <= maxGain. Roles that work mostly with people get narrow, low ranges.

pricing._comment: Claude plan prices in USD, from claude.com/pricing (checked 17 November 2026; 'Price and plans are subject to change'). Seats are counted per resource line as the line's peak AI FTE rounded up to whole people, paid in whole months for the weeks the line is active on the AI timeline.

enterprise.label: Claude Enterprise (token based)
enterprise.note: Seat price plus usage at API rates; usage uses the token rates per role. The 20-seat minimum applies to the organisation's contract, not per project.

team.label: Claude Team (seat based)
team.note: Min uses annual billing, max monthly billing. Seats have weekly usage limits; heavy agentic use can hit them.

individual.label: Claude Individual (Max 5x – 20x)
individual.note: Min puts everyone on Max, max puts everyone on Ultra (the 20x plan). Monthly billing only. Individual plans are bought per person.

dayRates._comment: Reserved for a later release (human cost). Not used by the MVP calculation.

survey.question: Number of integration points
survey.help: How many external systems the solution must exchange data with.

survey.question: Integration complexity
levels: Mix including asynchronous or legacy interfaces
survey.help: The hardest kind of interface among those integrations.

survey.question: Regulation
levels: Heavy regulation with audit or certification
survey.help: The strictest regulation the solution and its delivery must comply with.

survey.question: Mission criticality
survey.help: What happens to the client's business if the system is down.

survey.question: Importance of UX
levels: A differentiator, with a dedicated design system or user research
survey.help: How much the success of the solution depends on its user experience.

survey.question: Greenfield or legacy
levels: Modernization of a documented legacy system
Modernization of an undocumented legacy system

survey.question: Data migration
survey.help: Data that must be moved from existing systems into the new one.

survey.question: Security and data residency
levels: Strict: in-country or on-premises models required
survey.help: Constraints on where data and AI models may run.

survey.question: Clarity of requirements in the RFP
survey.help: How well the RFP defines what must be built.

survey.question: Tech stack familiarity
survey.help: How common the required technologies are.

survey.question: Client dependencies and approval cycles
survey.help: How quickly the client can decide and approve.

survey.question: Testing and compliance evidence required
survey.help: The testing evidence the client requires beyond normal testing.

surveyLinks._comment: Q2 depends on Q1: level 0 of each means 'no integrations'. Q1 at level 0 sets Q2 to level 0; Q1 above 0 makes Q2's level 0 unavailable.

weights._comment: Weight 0–3 per question and role: how much that factor limits AI gain for that role.
